standard_prerequisites.name: n-truncated simplicial object
standard_prerequisites.statement: A sequence of objects U_0, ..., U_n with face and degeneracy maps satisfying the simplicial identities, regarded as a functor on the category of finite non-empty ordinals of size at most n+1.
standard_prerequisites.use: The face maps and the identities are what the tuple condition in the statement and the verification in the proof use (source lines 2556-2563, 2620-2638).

standard_prerequisites.name: Limit over the truncated simplex category
standard_prerequisites.statement: The limit of a truncated simplicial object over the opposite of the category of maps [k] -> [n+1] with k <= n, presented as the set of compatible families.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the right-hand side of the statement and the object compared with the representing tuple (source lines 2568, 2573-2580).

standard_prerequisites.name: Representable functor
standard_prerequisites.statement: A contravariant functor to sets is representable by an object when there is a natural bijection between its values and the morphisms into that object.
standard_prerequisites.use: The hypothesis of representability is what lets the proof compare the two functors pointwise on an arbitrary object T (source lines 2565-2566, 2581-2600).

core_obligations: Identify the limit with the functor of compatible families: show that the limit over the truncated simplex category represents the functor sending T to the set of families indexed by the maps [k] -> [n+1] with k <= n, compatible with composition (source lines 2573-2580).

Relate the two descriptions: using representability, construct a map from the representing object to the limit, that is, from the tuple (f_0, ..., f_{n+1}) satisfying the identities to a compatible family, and define the family by restricting the tuple along the maps [k] -> [n+1] (source lines 2581-2615).

Construct the inverse and verify compatibility: given a compatible family, produce the missing component indexed by the identity of [n+1] and check the simplicial identities by factorising an arbitrary simplex map as a composite through an intermediate index and using the compatibility of the family together with the computation of the induced map on the composite index (source lines 2616-2638).

proof_roadmap.step: Rewrite the limit as the functor of compatible families indexed by truncated simplex maps.
Use representability to pass from a representing tuple to a compatible family.
Build the inverse by producing the missing component and verify the simplicial identities via a factorisation.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-formula-limit at source lines 2553-2570: for an n-truncated simplicial object U of a category C and the contravariant functor sending T to the set of (n+2)-tuples of maps T -> U_n satisfying the n+1 simplicial identities, if that functor is representable then its representing object is the limit of U over the opposite of the truncated simplex category over [n+1]. The proof at source lines 2572-2642 is a substantial comparison of two descriptions of the same functor. It must first write the limit as the set of compatible families indexed by the maps [k] -> [n+1] with k <= n, then construct maps from a representing object to that limit and back, and finally check compatibility. The constructive part is the interesting half: an element of the limit gives a family, and the proof has to manufacture, out of the family and a chosen representing tuple, the value at the extra index [n+1] -> [n+1] and then verify the simplicial identities by a factorisation argument through a chosen simplex map, computing U(psi) applied to the value at an index as the value at the composite index. The statement records none of the indexing bookkeeping. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
